uncited: **Branch Unification:** Divergent branches from different ray quadrants or entry points are eliminated to maintain SIMD efficiency, typically by permuting axes or unifying logic so all threads in a warp execute the same instruction stream .

**Memory Coalescing and Caching:** Global memory access patterns are coalesced, often using Structure of Arrays (SoA) layouts for ray data and caching voxel tiles in shared memory for threads accessing nearby voxels .
**Occupancy Management:** Shader occupancy is critical; high register allocation and excessive state carried across loops reduce concurrent warps and cause memory stalls .
Optimizations reduce register pressure and deduplicate calculations .
**Implicit Clipping:** Expensive explicit clipping is avoided by structuring tests so out-of-bounds accesses return sentinel values (e.g., zero depth) that naturally terminate iteration .
